title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026
official_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026
summary: This is the annual defense authorization law, which sets policy and authorizes funding levels for the entire Department of Defense for fiscal year 2026, plus the Energy Department's nuclear-weapons work, military construction, and the armed forces' personnel and health programs. This year's version also carries full-year authorizations for the State Department, the intelligence agencies, and the Coast Guard, and a large 'Other Matters' division covering outbound-investment screening, development finance, and more. It does not itself spend money; it authorizes and directs how defense money may be used.
brief: Authorizes fiscal year 2026 funding and policy for the Department of Defense, nuclear-weapons programs, military construction, and personnel, and carries State, intelligence, and Coast Guard authorizations plus other national-security measures.

top_lines.headline: Defense Authorizations
subs: Authorizes procurement, research and development, operations, and maintenance for the armed forces
Sets military personnel end strengths, pay, benefits, and health-care policy
Includes space, cyberspace, and strategic-programs authorizations

top_lines.headline: Nuclear, Construction, and Allied Programs
subs: Authorizes the Energy Department's national-security and nuclear-weapons programs
Authorizes military construction across the services, including specific projects
$1.58B authorized for construction at Naval Station Norfolk; $1.04B at Portsmouth Naval Shipyard

top_lines.headline: Beyond the Pentagon
subs: Carries the State Department and Intelligence authorization acts for 2026 and the Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2025
Enacts the Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act of 2025
Reauthorizes the U.S. development-finance agency, raising its liability cap to $205B

likelihoodReason: Signed into law on December 18, 2025 as Public Law 119-60. The annual National Defense Authorization Act is considered must-pass legislation and is enacted every year with bipartisan support.

sections.label: Division A — Department of Defense Authorizations

items.main: Authorizes Department of Defense programs and sets defense policy across seventeen titles for fiscal year 2026.
items.detail: The division authorizes procurement (Title I); research, development, test, and evaluation (Title II); operation and maintenance (Title III); military personnel end strengths (Title IV) and personnel policy (Title V); compensation and benefits (Title VI); health care (Title VII); acquisition policy and reform (Titles VIII and XVIII); department organization (Title IX); general provisions (Title X); civilian personnel (Title XI); matters relating to foreign nations (Title XII); cyberspace matters (Title XV); and space, strategic programs, and intelligence (Title XVI). Specific funding levels are set in the Division D funding tables.

sections.label: Divisions B & C — Military Construction and Energy Department National Security

items.main: Authorizes military construction and the Energy Department's national-security and nuclear programs.
items.detail: Division B authorizes military construction for the Army, Navy, Air Force, and defense agencies, international programs, Guard and Reserve facilities, and base realignment and closure activities — including named projects such as $1.58B for Naval Station Norfolk and $1.04B for Portsmouth Naval Shipyard. Division C authorizes the Energy Department's national-security programs (nuclear weapons activities), the Defense Nuclear Facilities Safety Board, the naval petroleum reserves, and the Maritime Administration.

sections.label: Divisions E, F & G — State, Intelligence, and Coast Guard Authorizations

items.main: Carries full-year authorization acts for the State Department, the intelligence community, and the Coast Guard.
items.detail: Division E is the Department of State Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, covering organization, workforce, information security and cyber diplomacy, public diplomacy, and diplomatic security. Division F is the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, including a title on artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies. Division G is the Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2025, addressing Coast Guard organization and personnel, shipping and navigation, oil-pollution response, and sexual assault and harassment response.

items.main: Carries non-defense national-security measures, including outbound-investment screening and development-finance reauthorization.
items.detail: Division H enacts the Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act of 2025 (Title LXXXV), establishing screening of certain U.S. investments abroad. The DFC Modernization and Reauthorization Act of 2025 (Title LXXXVII) reauthorizes the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation, raising its maximum contingent liability to $205B and authorizing $5B for its Equity Investment Account for fiscal years 2026 through 2031. The division also covers financial services, judiciary, foreign affairs, and oceanic and atmospheric matters.

underreported.section: Title LXXXV — Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act of 2025
underreported.summary: The defense authorization carries a standalone law establishing a federal regime to screen certain outbound U.S. investments for national-security risk.
underreported.why_unreported: Carried inside the defense authorization rather than as a freestanding bill, this title creates an investment-screening framework whose subject is economic and financial regulation rather than defense authorization.

underreported.section: Title LXXXVII — DFC Maximum Contingent Liability
underreported.summary: The bill raises the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation's maximum contingent liability outstanding at any one time to $205B in the aggregate, and authorizes $5B for its Equity Investment Account through fiscal year 2031.
underreported.why_unreported: This expansion of a development-finance agency's lending and equity-investment capacity sits within the defense authorization's 'Other Matters' division, separate from any defense program.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Grassley
featured_quotes.text: I understand that representatives of the Russian Orthodox Church are on Capitol Hill this week falsely claiming persecution by the Ukrainian Government. This is because of a law requiring churches in Ukraine to stop taking directions from the patriarch in Moscow, who was a KGB agent and reports directly to Vladimir Putin. Two years ago, I met with Ukrainian faith leaders in my office--about 30 of them--from many backgrounds, including Orthodox, Catholic, Evangelical, Jewish, and Muslim.

gaps: The bill authorizes defense programs and policy but does not itself appropriate the money, which depends on a separate defense appropriations bill.
The bill sets authorization levels through the Division D funding tables but, in this top-level pass, the overall dollar total is the sum of those tables rather than a single stated figure.
The bill carries State, intelligence, and Coast Guard authorizations but does not consolidate their separate authorization cycles into the defense schedule.
The bill enacts an outbound-investment screening regime but, in the portion reviewed, leaves the detailed covered-transaction definitions to implementing regulations.
